cluster_summary: A cluster of vulnerabilities in error page generation where user-controlled input is embedded without escaping (leading to XSS), exception stack traces are exposed (information disclosure), and an unbounded cache keyed by error messages leads to denial of service.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Apply HTML entity encoding (e.g., htmlEscape, StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4) to user-controlled strings before inserting them into error responses..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Missing HTML escaping in error messages
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Apply HTML entity encoding (e.g., htmlEscape, StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4) to user-controlled strings before inserting them into error responses.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Apply HTML entity encoding (e.g., htmlEscape, StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4) to user-controlled strings before inserting them into error responses.
sub_patterns.name: Missing HTML escaping in error messages
sub_patterns.root_cause: Error page rendering code assumes that the error message and stack trace strings are safe to embed directly into an HTML template without escaping. No HTML entity encoding is applied to user-controlled strings, allowing characters like '<' and '&' to be interpreted as markup.
